qAndA.answer: The instructor highlights the need for a large clamp to gently but firmly hold the flask, preventing it from moving or falling during the vacuum filtration process.
qAndA.question: Why does the instructor emphasize using a large clamp to secure the vacuum flask?

qAndA.answer: The instructor wets the filter paper to help it adhere to the Buchner funnel and prevent it from lifting up due to the suction created by the vacuum.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of wetting down the filter paper before pouring the solution?

qAndA.answer: Rinsing the flask ensures that any remaining solid particles are transferred onto the filter paper for complete collection.
qAndA.question: Why does the instructor rinse the flask with a wash bottle after pouring the initial solution?

qAndA.answer: The instructor utilizes a rubber policeman, a flexible spatula-like tool, to gently scrape and transfer the sample without damaging the filter paper or the watch glass.
qAndA.question: What tool does the instructor use to transfer the filtered solid from the Buchner funnel to the watch glass?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello everyone, today I'm going to show you how to do vacuum filtration using a luchiner
funnel.
To set up your luchiner funnel apparatus, first take your ring stand, then attach clamps.
Make sure that you have one of the large clamps so you will be able to gently but firmly clamp
your vacuum flask in place.
Make sure that you have your vacuum flask clamped into place before you continue with
your setup.
Next, take the rubber disc and place it on top of the flask with the lip facing up.
Then take your bugner funnel and making sure you have both pieces, gently place it on
top of the rubber disc.
This is your filter paper.
Place the filter paper inside the bugner funnel, then take one end of your vacuum tubing
and attach to the glass arm of the vacuum flask.
It's maybe a bit difficult but by twisting you should be able to get it on.
Then take the other end and attach it to the arm of the faucet.
Again twist it to get it on.
Now your bugner apparatus is all set up.
To start turn on the suction by turning on the faucet.
But do not turn it on too high.
Then take your wash bottle, you can wet down the filter paper.
This ensures that it does not lift up when you put this solution in it.
Now you can gently pour your solution containing your solid onto the filter paper.
You may have to rinse your flask out again in order to get all of the solid out.
Then you simply wait until all of the liquid drains and your sample begins to look dry.
You may be asked to rinse your crystals with some cold solution.
Do this gently to avoid lifting the filter paper up.
In order to get your crystals as dry as possible, you can gently but firmly press down on the
funnel to ensure a better vacuum.
Then when you are finished turn off the vacuum and remove the funnel from the apparatus.
In order to get your sample onto a watch glass, use a rubber policeman.
Gently scrape the sample from the filter paper onto your watch glass.
Try to get as much sample as possible.
The rubber policeman allows you to go into the corners and the sides quite effectively.
Now you know how to do a proper vacuum filtration using a bucner funnel.
Good luck and have fun!
